title: Persistent nonlinear Hall effect driven by parallel field across a topological phase transition and intraband sign-reversing integer quantum Hall effect
authors: Suheel Ahmad Malik, M. A. H. Ahsan, SK Firoz Islam
abstract: We investigate the linear and nonlinear Hall effects in a two-dimensional Rashba spin-orbit coupled nodal ring electronic system. We consider both the cases of linear Hall effect, the Berry curvature induced anomalous Hall and the perpendicular magnetic field-induced integer quantum Hall effect. We observe that the system exhibits a topological gap along the boundary of the nodal ring that strongly depends on the radius of the nodal ring and the strength of the Rashba spin-orbit interaction, resulting in the quantum anomalous Hall effect. Subsequently, we include a perpendicular uniform magnetic field and obtain the exact Landau levels that exhibit sign reversal in the slope with magnetic field around the ring boundary. This causes a sign reversal in the quantum Hall conductivity in the same band by tuning the magnetic field. Most importantly, we also show that when the magnetic field is strictly parallel to the system, it can induce an anisotropy to the Berry curvature that leads to the emergence of the nonlinear Hall effect. Additionally, tuning the parallel field can close and reopen the topological gap, resulting in the reverse topological phase transition from the topological Chern insulator to a trivial insulator. The nonlinear Hall effect remains persistent in both phases, but its dependence on the chemical potential exhibits distinct signatures. Noticeably, the nonlinear Hall response exhibits a sign-changing peak structure in Chern insulating phase whereas it displays a single-sign response in trivial insulating phase. These distinct signatures suggest that nonlinear Hall can serve as a probe to study such a topological phase transition.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes magnetotransport in a 2D nodal ring system, demonstrating how applying a parallel magnetic field can drive the system through a topological phase transition. The key finding is that the nonlinear Hall effect remains measurable and exhibits distinct, characteristic signatures in both the topological and trivial insulating phases, making it a powerful diagnostic tool for such transitions.
main_problem: The study investigates the linear and nonlinear Hall effects in a 2D Rashba spin-orbit coupled nodal ring system, specifically examining how the nonlinear Hall effect can serve as a robust probe for topological phase transitions.
main_result: The nonlinear Hall effect persists across a topological phase transition (Chern insulator to trivial insulator) induced by an in-plane magnetic field, exhibiting distinct sign-changing signatures in the topological phase versus a single-sign response in the trivial phase.
method: The analysis uses semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory and calculates the second-order anomalous Hall response using the Berry curvature dipole (BCD) density.
model_or_system: The model is a two-dimensional Rashba spin-orbit coupled nodal ring electronic system, whose Hamiltonian is modified by both perpendicular and parallel magnetic fields.
key_observables: Nonlinear Hall conductivity, topological gap closing/reopening, Berry curvature dipole (BCD), and the sign of the quantum Hall conductivity.
important_parameters: Rashba SOC strength ($\alpha$), nodal ring radius ($R$), and the strength of the parallel magnetic field ($B_{||}$).
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on the relaxation time approximation for the Boltzmann equation and assume the nonlinear Hall response is dominated by the intra-band BCD.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy spectrum showing gap closing/reopening, and plots display the Berry curvature density and the BCD for both the Chern insulating and trivial insulating phases.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing linear and anomalous Hall effects (including IQHE with perpendicular fields) to introducing the parallel field, which induces the nonlinear Hall effect and drives the topological phase transition, culminating in the diagnostic comparison of the nonlinear response across the transition.
why_interesting: The concept of using a nonlinear transport coefficient (like the nonlinear Hall effect) as a robust, measurable probe for characterizing topological phase transitions is highly relevant for experimental condensed matter physics.

The same LL undergoes spin sign reversal upon a change in the magnetic ﬁeld. Parameters taken are ǫR2 = 0.03 eV and α = 10−11 eV-m

The corresponding BCDs are plotted in (b) and (d), respectively. We plot only Dxz component of the Berry curvature dipole (BCD) as the other components are zero.
